notes:
The package serves the card's models[0], the MJCF scene a1.xml of gh.vikashplus/unitree_sim, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode; the model is read in place from the read-only clone at 21b5524e7c5586565de5e789e94bb69efd36db69 and is neither copied nor imported. cap.world.step.v1 writes data.ctrl bounded per actuator by the model's 12 actuator ctrlrange intervals (a1.xml:127-138); cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults (qpos0) and takes no seed; the world state is time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms and seed. The card's other two scenes, aliengo.xml and laikago.xml, are named in facts.md but not served (one package per repository, models[0] only). RISK: the package is a simulator, not a physical mobile base: it has no hardware backend, no path to a robot, the card's expected_mode is simulated and its risk_floor is R0, and the catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are R0; no physical effect is modelled or claimed. NOT COVERED: MuJoCo itself, which was not installed and cannot be installed where the gate ran (no network, no pip). The fake backend (fake.py) is a pure-Python stand-in for the mujoco library; it parses the MJCF text (including basic_scene.xml and the default classes) for the 12 actuator control ranges, 19 qpos, 18 qvel and the free-joint start pose (torso z=0.45, a1.xml:36), but it integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated hinge, does not integrate the free base, loads no mesh or texture, and resolves no contact, actuator, equality or tendon dynamics. The model sets no <option timestep>, so the stand-in uses MuJoCo's library default 2 ms as a placeholder (marked in fake.py); no trajectory was compared with the real engine and nothing was validated against Unitree hardware. EXPECTED WARNINGS: G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND (the fake backend is the stand-in mujoco module, so there is no native call log and no fake surface to compare), and G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the integer/quantity inputs the bridge derives (ticks, action.ctrl[*], seed); no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. This package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json authored_by is the model, reviewed_by stays null); it is checked on the fake backend only and no human review or hardware run is claimed. No extension capability ids were used, so there are no catalogue_requests. The final gate run after the provenance edits printed this same digest.
